# Discussion

**Why d-CCSSBU Charts for CV Data?** Distribution-free (nonparametric) control charts have been extensively studied [@Janacek1997MedianChart; @Chakraborti2001NPC; @Chakraborti2004DFCC; @Chakraborti2009precedence; @Chakraborti2019NPC; @Bakir2004SR; @Nelson1982; @Rocke1989Robust; @Ferrell1953; @Amin1995SignChart]. Quantile-based approaches were discussed in [@Parzen1979NSDM] and applied in [@Grimshaw1997QCC; @Zheng2014Quantile], while MAD-based charts were proposed in [@AbuShawiesh2008MAD; @Adekeye2012MSRCC]. These methods construct control charts using statistics such as means, medians, standard deviations, MADs, ranges, or combined quantiles together with their corresponding control limits. However, as demonstrated in [@Yang2026dccssbu], direct application of $\bar{X}$-$S$ charts and distribution-free median-MAD charts may generate excessive OOC signals because they were developed for homogeneous one-cluster processes, whereas CV data are inherently multiclustered.

A potential alternative is the KDE approach used in [@Yang2026sln] to estimate the $0.99865-$quantile as UCL. That approach was suitable for capability analysis because it was based on a large pooled dataset of USL-normalized individual observations. In control-chart applications, however, the reference distribution is constructed from event-level statistics such as event medians and MADs, resulting in a substantially smaller effective sample size. Furthermore, CV data frequently contain ND-dominated events, repeated observations, and events with zero MAD values. KDE-based estimation of extreme upper-tail quantiles may therefore overestimate the required UCL and reduce OOC detection sensitivity.

Methods based on parametric modeling of censored data, such as the MLE- and ROS-based approaches discussed in [@Walsh2022a; @Walsh2022b], were not adopted because they require distributional assumptions and reliable estimation of model parameters. Such assumptions may not always be easy to verify for multicluster CV data containing substantial proportions of ND observations and heterogeneous cluster structures. Since the objective of the present study is to develop a distribution-free monitoring framework, a nonparametric resampling approach was considered more appropriate.

Consequently, the proposed d-CCSSBU framework employs a stratified smoothed bootstrap approach. Stratification preserves the underlying sampling procedure  while smoothing avoids degeneracy caused by repeated observations and zero-MAD events. Together, these properties provide a practical distribution-free solution for multicluster CV data that is not readily addressed by conventional one-cluster SPC, KDE-based extreme-quantile estimation, or parametric censored-data approaches.

**Generalization of Conventional Control Charts.** An important theoretical property of the proposed framework is that conventional control charts become a special case. When the data are homogeneous and form a single cluster ($q=1$), the recommended value is necessarily $d=1$, reducing the procedure to a conventional distribution-free chart calibrated from a representative in-control dataset. The Mic data from Equipment A illustrate this property, where the Poisson $u$ chart and d-CCSSBU charts produced highly similar conclusions.

**Rationale of the d-Selection Algorithm.** For any candidate value of the heterogeneity index $d$, a reproducible d-CCSSBU-L chart and d-CCSSBU-S chart can be constructed. The d-CCSSBU-L chart always monitors event medians, whereas the d-CCSSBU-S chart always monitors event MAD values. These event-level monitoring statistics do not depend on the selected value of $d$. Furthermore, the robustness properties of the median and MAD statistics and the statistical properties of bootstrap-based procedures have been well established in the SPC and statistical literature [@Montgomery2020; @Qiu2014spc; @Chakraborti2019]. Consequently, the principal methodological question addressed in this study is not the construction of the monitoring statistics themselves, but the selection of an appropriate calibration structure through the choice of $d$. Different values of $d$ do not alter the charted statistical points. Instead, they alter the calibration datasets used for estimation of the control limits, which remain a fundamental component of all control-chart methodologies. The proposed d-selection procedure addresses this question through a hierarchical optimization framework. First, ND-event protection is applied because ND events represent acceptable and typically best-quality cleaning outcomes. Candidate values of $d$ that classify ND events as OOC are considered scientifically inconsistent and are excluded from further consideration. Second, conditional Stage 3A protection is applied. Stage 3A serves a role analogous to Phase I SPC, in which accumulated observations are assumed to represent the provisional in-control baseline and are used to establish the monitoring structure. Consequently, candidate values of $d$ that avoid Stage 3A OOC classifications are preferred because they remain consistent with the assumed baseline condition. However, Stage 3A protection is not imposed unconditionally. When all candidate values of $d$ produce Stage 3A OOC signals, the signals are retained and investigated as potentially genuine process anomalies rather than eliminated through further calibration adjustment. Third, benchmark-referenced OOC detection performance and heterogeneity retention are applied. Conventional $\bar X$ and $S$ charts are used as benchmark references for evaluating the relative ARL$_1$ performance of admissible candidate values of $d$. When one or more admissible candidates achieve benchmark-level or better ARL$_1$ performance across the complete shift range, the largest value of $d$ is selected because it retains the greatest amount of cluster heterogeneity while maintaining benchmark-level detection performance. Conversely, when no admissible candidate achieves benchmark-level performance across the complete shift range, the candidate with the most favorable relative ARL$_1$ performance is selected according to Rule 3. If multiple candidates provide equivalent relative ARL$_1$ performance, preference is again given to the largest value of $d$. This principle jointly considers benchmark-referenced OOC detection performance and retention of cluster heterogeneity within the calibration structure. 

Accordingly, the selected value of $d$ should not be interpreted as an unknown population parameter requiring statistical estimation. Rather, it should be interpreted as the solution to a constrained calibration-design problem defined by ND-event protection, conditional Stage 3A protection, ARL$_1$ performance requirements, and the objective of maximizing admissible heterogeneity.

The d-selection procedure should therefore be viewed as a reproducible hierarchical optimization framework rather than an ad hoc heuristic. Moreover, the calibration-dataset construction procedure is fully deterministic because cluster ordering, event ordering, tie-breaking rules, admissibility assessment, and final candidate selection are all explicitly defined. Once calibration has been finalized (Case 1, Case 3, or Case 4 of Step 9), the selected calibration dataset, recommended value of $d$, and resulting control limits remain fixed throughout Stage 3B monitoring and are not altered by subsequent accumulation of monitoring data. Consequently, the monitoring framework provides a stable and reproducible reference structure for ongoing process monitoring. Recalibration or retraining is required only when the existing calibration dataset is no longer representative of the current process, such as when new clusters emerge, calibration data are revised, process conditions change, or other circumstances described in the section of recalibration. In the absence of such retraining triggers, repeated application of the methodology yields the same recommended value of $d$, calibration structure, and control limits.


**$3\sigma$ Poisson $u$ Chart or Exact Poisson-Quantile $u$ Chart?** The Mic data from Equipment A highlight an important distinction between the conventional three-sigma Poisson $u$ chart and the exact Poisson-quantile $u$ chart. The exact chart is distributionally correct because its UCL is obtained directly from the Poisson quantile. In contrast, the conventional chart uses a normal approximation to the Poisson distribution. The normal approximation to a Poisson distribution generally improves as the Poisson mean increases because the distribution becomes less discrete and more symmetric. This behavior is illustrated by the Poisson probability mass functions presented in [pp.42-43, @rice2007mathematical] for $\lambda=0.1$, $1$, $5$, and $10$, where the distributions become increasingly bell-shaped as $\lambda$ increases.  A commonly used rule of thumb is that the normal approximation becomes adequate when the Poisson mean is approximately 5 or greater. However, Mic data typically contain very low counts, and the estimated event-level Poisson means are frequently less than 1. For Equipment A, the estimated event-level Poisson mean was only $\lambda_t=p_t\bar{u}=0.10$.

Under such low-count conditions, the discrete and right-skewed nature of the Poisson distribution remains pronounced, causing the exact Poisson-quantile UCL to be substantially larger than the corresponding normal-approximation UCL. This behavior was observed for Equipment A, where the conventional three-sigma Poisson $u$ chart produced a UCL of 2.0974, whereas the exact Poisson-quantile $u$ chart produced a UCL of 4.0. Consequently, the conventional chart provided a more stringent monitoring threshold and was more consistent with the d-CCSSBU-L and d-CCSSBU-S charts.

Both charts produced the same stability conclusion for Equipment A because no observations exceeded either control limit. Nevertheless, the comparison remains informative because it demonstrates the impact of low-count Mic data on Poisson control-limit construction. For Equipment A, the exact Poisson-quantile approach produced a substantially larger UCL than the conventional three-sigma approach, reflecting the discreteness and right-skewness of the Poisson distribution at very small event-level means.

\textcolor{blue}{The exact Poisson-quantile $u$ chart is therefore useful as a distributionally exact reference and sensitivity-analysis tool for evaluating the impact of the normal approximation. However, from a process-monitoring perspective, the conventional three-sigma Poisson $u$ chart provides a lower UCL and consequently greater sensitivity to potential microbial excursions. This increased sensitivity is accompanied by a corresponding increase in the in-control false-alarm rate. For Equipment A, the realized in-control performance of the conventional three-sigma chart was approximately $\mathrm{ARL}_0=214$, compared with the nominal design value of $ARL_0=740$, whereas the exact Poisson-quantile chart yielded approximately $\mathrm{ARL}_0=6466$. Thus, the improved sensitivity of the conventional chart arises from accepting more frequent false alarms, while the exact chart achieves substantially stronger false-alarm protection at the cost of a more conservative monitoring threshold.}

\textcolor{blue}{In practice, the choice between the two charts depends on the intended balance between detection sensitivity and false-alarm tolerance. The exact Poisson-quantile chart is more faithful to the underlying discrete Poisson distribution and is useful for understanding the effect of distributional discreteness when counts are extremely small. The conventional three-sigma chart, however, provides earlier detection of potential microbial excursions and showed closer agreement with the d-CCSSBU-L and d-CCSSBU-S charts developed in this study. For these reasons, the conventional three-sigma Poisson $u$ chart is recommended as the primary benchmark chart, while the exact Poisson-quantile chart is retained as a useful reference for evaluating the sensitivity-false-alarm trade-off in low-count microbial monitoring applications.}


**Why Bootstrap Synthetic Events Rather Than Historical Cleaning Events?** \textcolor{blue}{The proposed CCSSB procedure uses sampling locations, rather than complete historical cleaning events, as the bootstrap sampling units. Specifically, one observation is sampled from each sampling-location stratum and the sampled observations are combined to form a synthetic cleaning event. This design was motivated primarily by the limited number of cleaning events typically available in cleaning-validation datasets. Complete-event resampling is restricted to the finite set of historically observed events and therefore provides a limited empirical population for estimating the extreme upper tail required for control-limit estimation. In contrast, location-stratified resampling uses the location-specific empirical distributions to generate a substantially larger variety of plausible synthetic cleaning events while preserving the predefined sampling-plan structure and the observed residue distribution at each sampling location.}

\textcolor{blue}{The objective of the proposed bootstrap is therefore not to reconstruct individual historical cleaning events, but to approximate the distribution of the event-level monitoring statistics under an in-control cleaning process. From an SPC perspective, a stable cleaning process can be viewed as repeatedly generating cleaning events from the same underlying process. Under this idealized setting, synthetic events constructed from the location-specific distributions provide plausible realizations of future in-control cleaning events. The tradeoff is that location-stratified resampling does not explicitly preserve the within-event relationships among sampling locations observed in individual historical cleaning events. Because common cleaning conditions may simultaneously influence multiple locations, this represents a potential limitation of the proposed bootstrap procedure.}

\textcolor{blue}{To evaluate the practical impact of this limitation, a sensitivity analysis was conducted using all available Equipment B data. The proposed location-stratified bootstrap was compared with complete-event bootstrap resampling, which preserves the observed sampling-location relationships within each historical event. The resulting $UCL_L$ and $UCL_S$ values and their relative differences are summarized in} @tbl-bootstrap-equipment-b.


```{r bootstrap_event_location_ucl_function}
#| echo: false
#| message: false
#| warning: false
bootstrap_event_location_ucl <- function(
    file,

    equipment_label = "Equipment B",
    sheets = c("DAR", "CAR", "Mic"),

    # Bootstrap design
    target_ARL0 = 740,
    B = 20000,
    seed = 123,

    # Input columns
    event_col = "Event",
    location_col = "Location",
    result_col = "Result",
    lod_col = "LOD",
    loq_col = "LOQ",
    usl_col = "USL",

    # Output controls
    keep_bootstrap_statistics = FALSE,
    save_table = FALSE,
    output_file = file.path(
      getwd(),
      "Equipment_B_event_vs_location_bootstrap_UCL.csv"
    )
) {

  # ============================================================
  # 0. Package and argument checks
  # ============================================================

  required_pkgs <- c(
    "readxl",
    "dplyr",
    "stringr",
    "matrixStats"
  )

  missing_pkgs <- required_pkgs[
    !(required_pkgs %in% rownames(installed.packages()))
  ]

  if (length(missing_pkgs) > 0) {
    stop(
      "Please install the following package(s): ",
      paste(missing_pkgs, collapse = ", ")
    )
  }

  if (!file.exists(file)) {
    stop("The input file does not exist: ", file)
  }

  if (target_ARL0 <= 1) {
    stop("target_ARL0 must be greater than 1.")
  }

  if (B < 1) {
    stop("B must be a positive integer.")
  }

  B <- as.integer(B)

  alpha <- 1 / target_ARL0
  ucl_probability <- 1 - alpha

  available_sheets <- readxl::excel_sheets(file)

  missing_sheets <- setdiff(
    sheets,
    available_sheets
  )

  if (length(missing_sheets) > 0) {
    stop(
      "The following requested worksheet(s) were not found: ",
      paste(missing_sheets, collapse = ", "),
      ". Available worksheets: ",
      paste(available_sheets, collapse = ", ")
    )
  }

  # ============================================================
  # 1. Helper functions
  # ============================================================

  mad_unscaled <- function(x) {

    x <- x[
      !is.na(x) &
        is.finite(x)
    ]

    if (length(x) == 0) {
      return(NA_real_)
    }

    med_x <- stats::median(
      x,
      na.rm = TRUE
    )

    stats::median(
      abs(x - med_x),
      na.rm = TRUE
    )
  }

  is_nd_result <- function(x) {

    x_chr <- trimws(
      toupper(
        as.character(x)
      )
    )

    x_chr %in% c(
      "ND",
      "N.D.",
      "N/D",
      "NON-DETECT",
      "NONDETECT",
      "NON DETECT",
      "NOT DETECT"
    )
  }

  extract_event_number <- function(x) {

    x_chr <- trimws(
      as.character(x)
    )

    x_num_direct <- suppressWarnings(
      as.numeric(x_chr)
    )

    x_num_extracted <- suppressWarnings(
      as.numeric(
        stringr::str_extract(
          x_chr,
          "\\d+$"
        )
      )
    )

    dplyr::case_when(
      !is.na(x_num_direct) ~ x_num_direct,
      !is.na(x_num_extracted) ~ x_num_extracted,
      TRUE ~ NA_real_
    )
  }

  fast_quantile <- function(x, probs) {

    x <- x[
      !is.na(x) &
        is.finite(x)
    ]

    if (length(x) == 0) {
      return(NA_real_)
    }

    as.numeric(
      stats::quantile(
        x = x,
        probs = probs,
        type = 7,
        na.rm = TRUE,
        names = FALSE
      )
    )
  }

  calculate_percent_difference <- function(
      location_value,
      event_value
  ) {

    if (
      is.na(location_value) ||
      is.na(event_value) ||
      !is.finite(location_value) ||
      !is.finite(event_value) ||
      event_value == 0
    ) {
      return(NA_real_)
    }

    100 * (
      location_value - event_value
    ) / event_value
  }

  # ============================================================
  # 2. Process one residue worksheet
  # ============================================================

  analyze_one_residue <- function(
      sheet_name,
      sheet_seed
  ) {

    message(
      "Analyzing ",
      equipment_label,
      ": ",
      sheet_name
    )

    # ----------------------------------------------------------
    # 2.1 Read worksheet
    # ----------------------------------------------------------

    dat_raw <- readxl::read_excel(
      path = file,
      sheet = sheet_name
    )

    dat_raw <- dat_raw |>
      dplyr::rename_with(
        ~ stringr::str_trim(.x)
      )

    result_col_actual <- result_col

    if (
      !(result_col_actual %in% names(dat_raw)) &&
        sheet_name %in% names(dat_raw)
    ) {
      result_col_actual <- sheet_name
    }

    required_cols <- c(
      event_col,
      location_col,
      result_col_actual,
      lod_col,
      loq_col,
      usl_col
    )

    missing_cols <- setdiff(
      required_cols,
      names(dat_raw)
    )

    if (length(missing_cols) > 0) {
      stop(
        "Worksheet ",
        sheet_name,
        " is missing required column(s): ",
        paste(missing_cols, collapse = ", ")
      )
    }

    # ----------------------------------------------------------
    # 2.2 Replace ND and conduct USL normalization
    # ----------------------------------------------------------

    normalized_data <- dat_raw |>
      dplyr::mutate(
        Equipment = equipment_label,

        ResidueType = sheet_name,

        Event = extract_event_number(
          .data[[event_col]]
        ),

        Location = trimws(
          as.character(
            .data[[location_col]]
          )
        ),

        Result_chr = trimws(
          as.character(
            .data[[result_col_actual]]
          )
        ),

        ND_flag = is_nd_result(
          Result_chr
        ),

        Result_raw = suppressWarnings(
          as.numeric(Result_chr)
        ),

        LOD = suppressWarnings(
          as.numeric(
            .data[[lod_col]]
          )
        ),

        LOQ = suppressWarnings(
          as.numeric(
            .data[[loq_col]]
          )
        ),

        USL = suppressWarnings(
          as.numeric(
            .data[[usl_col]]
          )
        ),

        Result_Replacement_Source =
          dplyr::case_when(
            ND_flag & !is.na(LOD) ~
              "ND replaced by LOD",

            ND_flag &
              is.na(LOD) &
              !is.na(LOQ) ~
              "ND replaced by LOQ",

            ND_flag &
              is.na(LOD) &
              is.na(LOQ) ~
              "Removed: ND with missing LOD and LOQ",

            !ND_flag &
              !is.na(Result_raw) ~
              "Observed Result",

            TRUE ~
              "Removed: missing or nonnumeric Result"
          ),

        Result_ND_Replaced =
          dplyr::case_when(
            ND_flag & !is.na(LOD) ~
              LOD,

            ND_flag &
              is.na(LOD) &
              !is.na(LOQ) ~
              LOQ,

            ND_flag &
              is.na(LOD) &
              is.na(LOQ) ~
              NA_real_,

            !ND_flag &
              !is.na(Result_raw) ~
              Result_raw,

            TRUE ~
              NA_real_
          )
      ) |>
      dplyr::filter(
        !is.na(Event),
        !is.na(Location),
        Location != "",
        !is.na(Result_ND_Replaced),
        is.finite(Result_ND_Replaced),
        !is.na(USL),
        is.finite(USL),
        USL > 0
      ) |>
      dplyr::mutate(
        Normalized =
          100 * Result_ND_Replaced / USL
      ) |>
      dplyr::filter(
        !is.na(Normalized),
        is.finite(Normalized)
      ) |>
      dplyr::arrange(
        Event,
        Location
      )

    if (nrow(normalized_data) == 0) {
      stop(
        "No usable observations remain in worksheet ",
        sheet_name,
        " after preprocessing."
      )
    }

    n_events <- dplyr::n_distinct(
      normalized_data$Event
    )

    n_locations <- dplyr::n_distinct(
      normalized_data$Location
    )

    if (n_events < 2) {
      stop(
        "Worksheet ",
        sheet_name,
        " must contain at least two usable events."
      )
    }

    if (n_locations < 1) {
      stop(
        "Worksheet ",
        sheet_name,
        " has no usable sampling locations."
      )
    }

    # ----------------------------------------------------------
    # 2.3 Check the sampling-location structure
    # ----------------------------------------------------------

    event_location_structure <- normalized_data |>
      dplyr::group_by(Event) |>
      dplyr::summarise(
        n_observations = dplyr::n(),

        n_locations =
          dplyr::n_distinct(Location),

        location_set = paste(
          sort(unique(Location)),
          collapse = " | "
        ),

        .groups = "drop"
      )

    n_distinct_location_sets <-
      dplyr::n_distinct(
        event_location_structure$location_set
      )

    if (n_distinct_location_sets > 1) {
      warning(
        "Worksheet ",
        sheet_name,
        " contains ",
        n_distinct_location_sets,
        " different event-level sampling-location sets. ",
        "The location-stratified bootstrap forms synthetic events ",
        "using all location strata represented in the worksheet, ",
        "whereas the event bootstrap preserves each historical ",
        "event's original sampling-location set."
      )
    }

    # ----------------------------------------------------------
    # 2.4 Calculate statistics for complete historical events
    # ----------------------------------------------------------

    event_statistics <- normalized_data |>
      dplyr::group_by(Event) |>
      dplyr::summarise(
        L_t = stats::median(
          Normalized,
          na.rm = TRUE
        ),

        S_t = mad_unscaled(
          Normalized
        ),

        n_observations = dplyr::n(),

        n_locations =
          dplyr::n_distinct(Location),

        n_ND = sum(
          ND_flag,
          na.rm = TRUE
        ),

        .groups = "drop"
      ) |>
      dplyr::filter(
        !is.na(L_t),
        is.finite(L_t),
        !is.na(S_t),
        is.finite(S_t)
      ) |>
      dplyr::arrange(Event)

    if (nrow(event_statistics) < 2) {
      stop(
        "Worksheet ",
        sheet_name,
        " has fewer than two usable complete-event statistics."
      )
    }

    # ==========================================================
    # 3. Unsmoothed location-stratified bootstrap
    # ==========================================================

    location_data <- split(
      normalized_data$Normalized,
      normalized_data$Location
    )

    location_data <- lapply(
      location_data,
      function(z) {
        z[
          !is.na(z) &
            is.finite(z)
        ]
      }
    )

    location_data <- location_data[
      lengths(location_data) > 0
    ]

    location_data <- location_data[
      sort(names(location_data))
    ]

    if (length(location_data) == 0) {
      stop(
        "No valid location strata remain for worksheet ",
        sheet_name,
        "."
      )
    }

    set.seed(
      sheet_seed + 1L
    )

    location_bootstrap_matrix <- matrix(
      NA_real_,
      nrow = B,
      ncol = length(location_data)
    )

    colnames(location_bootstrap_matrix) <-
      names(location_data)

    for (r in seq_along(location_data)) {

      z_r <- location_data[[r]]

      # Sample only observed normalized values.
      # No smoothing noise is added.
      location_bootstrap_matrix[, r] <-
        sample(
          x = z_r,
          size = B,
          replace = TRUE
        )
    }

    if (ncol(location_bootstrap_matrix) == 1) {

      L_location_boot <-
        location_bootstrap_matrix[, 1]

      S_location_boot <-
        rep(0, B)

    } else {

      L_location_boot <-
        matrixStats::rowMedians(
          location_bootstrap_matrix,
          na.rm = TRUE
        )

      location_absolute_deviations <-
        abs(
          sweep(
            x = location_bootstrap_matrix,
            MARGIN = 1,
            STATS = L_location_boot,
            FUN = "-"
          )
        )

      S_location_boot <-
        matrixStats::rowMedians(
          location_absolute_deviations,
          na.rm = TRUE
        )
    }

    UCL_L_location <- fast_quantile(
      L_location_boot,
      probs = ucl_probability
    )

    UCL_S_location <- fast_quantile(
      S_location_boot,
      probs = ucl_probability
    )

    # ==========================================================
    # 4. Complete-event bootstrap
    # ==========================================================

    set.seed(
      sheet_seed + 2L
    )

    sampled_event_rows <- sample.int(
      n = nrow(event_statistics),
      size = B,
      replace = TRUE
    )

    L_event_boot <-
      event_statistics$L_t[
        sampled_event_rows
      ]

    S_event_boot <-
      event_statistics$S_t[
        sampled_event_rows
      ]

    UCL_L_event <- fast_quantile(
      L_event_boot,
      probs = ucl_probability
    )

    UCL_S_event <- fast_quantile(
      S_event_boot,
      probs = ucl_probability
    )

    # ==========================================================
    # 5. Compare the resulting UCLs
    # ==========================================================

    Delta_UCL_L <-
      UCL_L_location -
      UCL_L_event

    Percent_Delta_UCL_L <-
      calculate_percent_difference(
        location_value = UCL_L_location,
        event_value = UCL_L_event
      )

    Delta_UCL_S <-
      UCL_S_location -
      UCL_S_event

    Percent_Delta_UCL_S <-
      calculate_percent_difference(
        location_value = UCL_S_location,
        event_value = UCL_S_event
      )

    comparison_row <- data.frame(
      ResidueType = sheet_name,

      n_events = nrow(event_statistics),

      n_locations =
        length(location_data),

      n_distinct_event_location_sets =
        n_distinct_location_sets,

      B = B,

      target_ARL0 = target_ARL0,

      alpha = alpha,

      UCL_L_location = UCL_L_location,

      UCL_L_event = UCL_L_event,

      Delta_UCL_L = Delta_UCL_L,

      Percent_Delta_UCL_L =
        Percent_Delta_UCL_L,

      UCL_S_location = UCL_S_location,

      UCL_S_event = UCL_S_event,

      Delta_UCL_S = Delta_UCL_S,

      Percent_Delta_UCL_S =
        Percent_Delta_UCL_S,

      stringsAsFactors = FALSE
    )

    location_strata_summary <- data.frame(
      ResidueType = sheet_name,

      Location = names(location_data),

      n = lengths(location_data),

      Median = vapply(
        location_data,
        stats::median,
        numeric(1),
        na.rm = TRUE
      ),

      MAD = vapply(
        location_data,
        mad_unscaled,
        numeric(1)
      ),

      Min = vapply(
        location_data,
        min,
        numeric(1),
        na.rm = TRUE
      ),

      Max = vapply(
        location_data,
        max,
        numeric(1),
        na.rm = TRUE
      ),

      stringsAsFactors = FALSE
    )

    details <- list(
      residue_type = sheet_name,

      normalized_data =
        normalized_data,

      event_statistics =
        event_statistics,

      event_location_structure =
        event_location_structure,

      location_strata_summary =
        location_strata_summary,

      UCL_L_location =
        UCL_L_location,

      UCL_S_location =
        UCL_S_location,

      UCL_L_event =
        UCL_L_event,

      UCL_S_event =
        UCL_S_event,

      comparison =
        comparison_row
    )

    if (keep_bootstrap_statistics) {

      details$bootstrap_statistics <- list(
        L_location = L_location_boot,
        S_location = S_location_boot,
        L_event = L_event_boot,
        S_event = S_event_boot
      )

    } else {

      details$bootstrap_statistics <- NULL
    }

    details
  }

  # ============================================================
  # 6. Analyze DAR, CAR, and Mic
  # ============================================================

  residue_results <- lapply(
    seq_along(sheets),
    function(i) {

      analyze_one_residue(
        sheet_name = sheets[i],
        sheet_seed = seed + 1000L * i
      )
    }
  )

  names(residue_results) <- sheets

  comparison_table <- dplyr::bind_rows(
    lapply(
      residue_results,
      function(x) {
        x$comparison
      }
    )
  )

  comparison_table <- comparison_table |>
    dplyr::mutate(
      dplyr::across(
        dplyr::starts_with("UCL_"),
        ~ round(.x, 6)
      ),

      dplyr::across(
        dplyr::starts_with("Delta_"),
        ~ round(.x, 6)
      ),

      dplyr::across(
        dplyr::starts_with("Percent_Delta_"),
        ~ round(.x, 3)
      )
    )

  if (save_table) {

    utils::write.csv(
      x = comparison_table,
      file = output_file,
      row.names = FALSE
    )

    message(
      "Comparison table saved to: ",
      output_file
    )
  }

  # ============================================================
  # 7. Return results
  # ============================================================

  output <- list(
    method =
      paste0(
        "Unsmoothed location-stratified bootstrap versus ",
        "complete-event bootstrap"
      ),

    equipment_label =
      equipment_label,

    file =
      file,

    sheets =
      sheets,

    target_ARL0 =
      target_ARL0,

    alpha =
      alpha,

    ucl_probability =
      ucl_probability,

    B =
      B,

    seed =
      seed,

    location_bootstrap_smoothing =
      FALSE,

    delta_definition =
      "Delta = UCL_location - UCL_event",

    percent_delta_definition =
      paste0(
        "Percent Delta = 100 * ",
        "(UCL_location - UCL_event) / UCL_event"
      ),

    comparison_table =
      comparison_table,

    residue_results =
      residue_results,

    output_file = if (save_table) {
      output_file
    } else {
      NA_character_
    }
  )

  class(output) <- c(
    "bootstrap_event_location_ucl",
    "list"
  )

  print(comparison_table)

  return(output)
}
```

```{r bootstrap_event_location_ucl_function_run}
#| echo: false
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| results: 'hide'

equipment_b_bootstrap_comparison <-
  bootstrap_event_location_ucl(
    file = file1,
    equipment_label = "Equipment B",
    sheets = c("DAR", "CAR", "Mic"),
    target_ARL0 = 740,
    B = 2000000,
    seed = 2345678,
    keep_bootstrap_statistics = FALSE,
    save_table = TRUE
  )
```

```{r tbl-bootstrap-equipment-b}
#| echo: false
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| tbl-cap: "location-stratified and complete-event bootstrap UCL for Equipment B."
#| tbl-label: tbl-bootstrap-equipment-b

bootstrap_equipment_b_table <-
  equipment_b_bootstrap_comparison$comparison_table |>
  dplyr::transmute(
    Residue = ResidueType,
    L_Loc = UCL_L_location,
    L_Evt = UCL_L_event,
    L_Diff = Delta_UCL_L,
    L_DiffPct = Percent_Delta_UCL_L,
    S_Loc = UCL_S_location,
    S_Evt = UCL_S_event,
    S_Diff = Delta_UCL_S,
    S_DiffPct = Percent_Delta_UCL_S
  )

bootstrap_equipment_b_table |>
  knitr::kable(
    format = "latex",
    booktabs = TRUE,
    digits = 4,
    align = c(
      "l",
      rep("r", 8)
    ),
    col.names = c(
      "Residue",
      "Loc.",
      "Event",
      "$\\Delta$",
      "$\\Delta\\%$",
      "Loc.",
      "Event",
      "$\\Delta$",
      "$\\Delta\\%$"
    ),
    escape = FALSE
  ) |>
  kableExtra::add_header_above(
    c(
      " " = 1,
      "$UCL_L$" = 4,
      "$UCL_S$" = 4
    ),
    escape = FALSE
  ) |>
  kableExtra::kable_styling(
    latex_options = c(
      "scale_down",
      "hold_position"
    ),
    position = "center",
    font_size = 8
  ) |>
  kableExtra::column_spec(
    column = 1,
    bold = TRUE
  )
```

\textcolor{blue}{For the event-level location statistic, the location-stratified bootstrap produced $UCL_L$ values that were equal to or lower than those obtained from complete-event resampling for DAR, CAR, and Mic. Thus, the proposed resampling procedure did not inflate the upper control limit for the location statistic in the investigated cleaning-validation data and produced an equal or more conservative location limit. The scale statistic was more sensitive to the choice of resampling unit. Although the location-stratified bootstrap produced a more conservative $UCL_S$ for DAR, the direction was reversed for CAR and Mic. These differences were particularly associated with the discrete structure of the genuine cleaning-validation data, including substantial ties and zero-MAD events resulting from replacement of ND observations by common LOD or LOQ values. Complete-event resampling preserves these structures exactly, whereas location-stratified resampling creates new combinations of observations across historical events.}

\textcolor{blue}{An additional simulation study was conducted to examine the same comparison under an idealized setting without the complications introduced by ND observations and within-event dependence. Ten sampling locations were generated independently from normal distributions with common variance $2^2$ and location-specific means ranging from 1.1 to 2.0, namely $N(1.1,2^2), N(1.2,2^2), \ldots, N(2.0,2^2)$. A total of 20,000 complete events were simulated directly from these known distributions. Separately, 100 simulated historical events were used to construct 10 empirical location strata, from which 20,000 synthetic events were generated using the location-stratified bootstrap. The resulting control limits are summarized in} @tbl-bootstrap-simulation.

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| message: false
#| warning: false

simulate_event_location_ucl <- function(
    n_historical_events = 100,
    n_locations = 10,
    location_means = seq(1.1, 2.0, by = 0.1),
    location_sd = 2,
    n_simulated_events = 20000,
    B = 20000,
    target_ARL0 = 740,
    seed = 123
) {

  # ------------------------------------------------------------
  # Argument checks
  # ------------------------------------------------------------

  if (length(location_means) != n_locations) {
    stop(
      "The length of location_means must equal n_locations."
    )
  }

  if (n_historical_events < 1) {
    stop("n_historical_events must be positive.")
  }

  if (n_simulated_events < 1) {
    stop("n_simulated_events must be positive.")
  }

  if (B < 1) {
    stop("B must be positive.")
  }

  if (target_ARL0 <= 1) {
    stop("target_ARL0 must be greater than 1.")
  }

  alpha <- 1 / target_ARL0
  ucl_probability <- 1 - alpha

  # ------------------------------------------------------------
  # Helper: unscaled MAD used in the CCSSBU procedure
  # ------------------------------------------------------------

  mad_unscaled <- function(x) {

    med_x <- median(
      x,
      na.rm = TRUE
    )

    median(
      abs(x - med_x),
      na.rm = TRUE
    )
  }

  fast_quantile <- function(x, probs) {

    as.numeric(
      stats::quantile(
        x = x,
        probs = probs,
        type = 7,
        na.rm = TRUE,
        names = FALSE
      )
    )
  }

  # ------------------------------------------------------------
  # Step 1. Generate 100 historical events.
  #
  # Each row represents one event.
  # Each column represents one sampling location.
  # ------------------------------------------------------------

  set.seed(seed)

  historical_data <- matrix(
    NA_real_,
    nrow = n_historical_events,
    ncol = n_locations
  )

  colnames(historical_data) <- paste0(
    "Location_",
    seq_len(n_locations)
  )

  for (r in seq_len(n_locations)) {

    historical_data[, r] <- stats::rnorm(
      n = n_historical_events,
      mean = location_means[r],
      sd = location_sd
    )
  }

  # ------------------------------------------------------------
  # Step 2. Simulate complete events directly from the known
  # location distributions.
  #
  # Because the locations are generated independently, each row
  # represents a complete event from the known event-generating
  # mechanism.
  # ------------------------------------------------------------

  simulated_event_data <- matrix(
    NA_real_,
    nrow = n_simulated_events,
    ncol = n_locations
  )

  colnames(simulated_event_data) <- paste0(
    "Location_",
    seq_len(n_locations)
  )

  for (r in seq_len(n_locations)) {

    simulated_event_data[, r] <- stats::rnorm(
      n = n_simulated_events,
      mean = location_means[r],
      sd = location_sd
    )
  }

  L_event <- apply(
    simulated_event_data,
    MARGIN = 1,
    FUN = median
  )

  S_event <- apply(
    simulated_event_data,
    MARGIN = 1,
    FUN = mad_unscaled
  )

  UCL_L_event <- fast_quantile(
    L_event,
    probs = ucl_probability
  )

  UCL_S_event <- fast_quantile(
    S_event,
    probs = ucl_probability
  )

  # ------------------------------------------------------------
  # Step 3. Construct G_1,...,G_10 from the 100 historical events.
  # ------------------------------------------------------------

  location_strata <- lapply(
    seq_len(n_locations),
    function(r) {
      historical_data[, r]
    }
  )

  names(location_strata) <- colnames(
    historical_data
  )

  # ------------------------------------------------------------
  # Step 4. Location-stratified empirical bootstrap.
  #
  # Sample one observation from each G_r and combine the sampled
  # values into a synthetic event. No smoothing noise is added.
  # ------------------------------------------------------------

  set.seed(seed + 1L)

  location_bootstrap_data <- matrix(
    NA_real_,
    nrow = B,
    ncol = n_locations
  )

  colnames(location_bootstrap_data) <- paste0(
    "Location_",
    seq_len(n_locations)
  )

  for (r in seq_len(n_locations)) {

    location_bootstrap_data[, r] <- sample(
      x = location_strata[[r]],
      size = B,
      replace = TRUE
    )
  }

  L_location <- apply(
    location_bootstrap_data,
    MARGIN = 1,
    FUN = median
  )

  S_location <- apply(
    location_bootstrap_data,
    MARGIN = 1,
    FUN = mad_unscaled
  )

  UCL_L_location <- fast_quantile(
    L_location,
    probs = ucl_probability
  )

  UCL_S_location <- fast_quantile(
    S_location,
    probs = ucl_probability
  )

  # ------------------------------------------------------------
  # Step 5. Compare the UCLs.
  # ------------------------------------------------------------

  Delta_L <-
    UCL_L_location -
    UCL_L_event

  Delta_S <-
    UCL_S_location -
    UCL_S_event

  Percent_Delta_L <-
    100 * Delta_L / UCL_L_event

  Percent_Delta_S <-
    100 * Delta_S / UCL_S_event

  comparison_table <- data.frame(
    Statistic = c(
      "L",
      "S"
    ),

    UCL_event = c(
      UCL_L_event,
      UCL_S_event
    ),

    UCL_location = c(
      UCL_L_location,
      UCL_S_location
    ),

    Delta = c(
      Delta_L,
      Delta_S
    ),

    Percent_Delta = c(
      Percent_Delta_L,
      Percent_Delta_S
    ),

    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )

  # ------------------------------------------------------------
  # Return all useful objects.
  # ------------------------------------------------------------

  result <- list(
    seed = seed,

    n_historical_events =
      n_historical_events,

    n_locations =
      n_locations,

    location_means =
      location_means,

    location_sd =
      location_sd,

    n_simulated_events =
      n_simulated_events,

    B =
      B,

    target_ARL0 =
      target_ARL0,

    alpha =
      alpha,

    ucl_probability =
      ucl_probability,

    historical_data =
      historical_data,

    location_strata =
      location_strata,

    simulated_event_statistics =
      data.frame(
        L_event = L_event,
        S_event = S_event
      ),

    location_bootstrap_statistics =
      data.frame(
        L_location = L_location,
        S_location = S_location
      ),

    UCL_L_event =
      UCL_L_event,

    UCL_S_event =
      UCL_S_event,

    UCL_L_location =
      UCL_L_location,

    UCL_S_location =
      UCL_S_location,

    comparison_table =
      comparison_table
  )

  class(result) <- c(
    "simulate_event_location_ucl",
    "list"
  )

  print(comparison_table)

  return(result)
}
```

 @tbl-bootstrap-simulation \textcolor{blue}{shows, under idealized setting, the location-stratified bootstrap closely approximated the control limits obtained from direct complete-event simulation and produced slightly lower $UCL_L$ and $UCL_S$ values. The simulation therefore supports the use of location-stratified resampling when the location-specific empirical distributions adequately represent the underlying in-control process.}


\textcolor{blue}{A correlated dataset consisting of 100 complete events and 10 sampling locations was first generated from the random-effects model $X_{ir}=\mu_r+E_i+\varepsilon_{ir}$, where $\mu_r=1.1,1.2,\ldots,2.0$, $E_i\sim N(0,1)$, and $\varepsilon_{ir}\sim N(0,3)$. Consequently, each location had marginal variance 4, while the within-event correlation between any two locations was 0.25. The location-stratified bootstrap generated 200,000 synthetic events by independently drawing one observation from each of the 10 empirical location strata. For comparison, the event-level bootstrap resampled 200,000 times from the 100 observed event-level pairs $(L_t,S_t)$. Control limits corresponding to the target $\mathrm{ARL}_0=740$ were then estimated from the respective bootstrap distributions and are summarized in} @tbl-bootstrap-simulation-multi.


```{r}
#| echo: false
#| message: false
#| warning: false

simulate_event_location_ucl <- function(
    n_historical_events = 100,
    n_locations = 10,
    location_means = seq(1.1, 2.0, by = 0.1),
    event_variance = 1,
    residual_variance = 3,
    B = 200000,
    target_ARL0 = 740,
    seed = 123
) {

  # ------------------------------------------------------------
  # Argument checks
  # ------------------------------------------------------------

  if (length(location_means) != n_locations) {
    stop(
      "The length of location_means must equal n_locations."
    )
  }

  if (n_historical_events < 2) {
    stop(
      "n_historical_events must be at least 2."
    )
  }

  if (n_locations < 2) {
    stop(
      "n_locations must be at least 2."
    )
  }

  if (event_variance < 0) {
    stop(
      "event_variance cannot be negative."
    )
  }

  if (residual_variance <= 0) {
    stop(
      "residual_variance must be positive."
    )
  }

  if (B < 1) {
    stop(
      "B must be positive."
    )
  }

  if (target_ARL0 <= 1) {
    stop(
      "target_ARL0 must be greater than 1."
    )
  }

  alpha <- 1 / target_ARL0
  ucl_probability <- 1 - alpha

  marginal_variance <-
    event_variance +
    residual_variance

  marginal_sd <-
    sqrt(marginal_variance)

  within_event_correlation <-
    event_variance /
    marginal_variance

  # ------------------------------------------------------------
  # Helper: unscaled MAD used in the CCSSBU procedure
  # ------------------------------------------------------------

  mad_unscaled <- function(x) {

    med_x <- median(
      x,
      na.rm = TRUE
    )

    median(
      abs(x - med_x),
      na.rm = TRUE
    )
  }

  fast_quantile <- function(x, probs) {

    as.numeric(
      stats::quantile(
        x = x,
        probs = probs,
        type = 7,
        na.rm = TRUE,
        names = FALSE
      )
    )
  }

  # ------------------------------------------------------------
  # Step 1. Generate 100 correlated historical events.
  #
  # Model:
  #
  # X_ir = mu_r + E_i + epsilon_ir,
  #
  # where
  #
  # E_i ~ N(0, event_variance)
  #
  # and
  #
  # epsilon_ir ~ N(0, residual_variance).
  #
  # Each row is one complete event.
  # Each column is one sampling location.
  # ------------------------------------------------------------

  set.seed(seed)

  event_effects <- stats::rnorm(
    n = n_historical_events,
    mean = 0,
    sd = sqrt(event_variance)
  )

  residual_errors <- matrix(
    stats::rnorm(
      n = n_historical_events * n_locations,
      mean = 0,
      sd = sqrt(residual_variance)
    ),
    nrow = n_historical_events,
    ncol = n_locations
  )

  historical_data <-
    residual_errors +
    event_effects +
    matrix(
      location_means,
      nrow = n_historical_events,
      ncol = n_locations,
      byrow = TRUE
    )

  colnames(historical_data) <- paste0(
    "Location_",
    seq_len(n_locations)
  )

  rownames(historical_data) <- paste0(
    "Event_",
    seq_len(n_historical_events)
  )

  # ------------------------------------------------------------
  # Step 2. Calculate the observed L_t and S_t values for the
  # 100 historical events.
  # ------------------------------------------------------------

  L_observed <- apply(
    historical_data,
    MARGIN = 1,
    FUN = median
  )

  S_observed <- apply(
    historical_data,
    MARGIN = 1,
    FUN = mad_unscaled
  )

  observed_event_statistics <- data.frame(
    Event = seq_len(n_historical_events),
    L = L_observed,
    S = S_observed
  )

  # ------------------------------------------------------------
  # Step 3. Construct G_1,...,G_10 from the 100 historical
  # events.
  # ------------------------------------------------------------

  location_strata <- lapply(
    seq_len(n_locations),
    function(r) {
      historical_data[, r]
    }
  )

  names(location_strata) <- colnames(
    historical_data
  )

  # ------------------------------------------------------------
  # Step 4. Location-stratified bootstrap.
  #
  # For each bootstrap replication, sample one observation from
  # each G_r. The 10 independently sampled location values are
  # combined to form one synthetic event.
  #
  # This procedure preserves each empirical location
  # distribution but does not preserve the within-event
  # dependence in the original data.
  # ------------------------------------------------------------

  set.seed(seed + 1L)

  location_bootstrap_data <- matrix(
    NA_real_,
    nrow = B,
    ncol = n_locations
  )

  colnames(location_bootstrap_data) <- paste0(
    "Location_",
    seq_len(n_locations)
  )

  for (r in seq_len(n_locations)) {

    location_bootstrap_data[, r] <- sample(
      x = location_strata[[r]],
      size = B,
      replace = TRUE
    )
  }

  L_location <- apply(
    location_bootstrap_data,
    MARGIN = 1,
    FUN = median
  )

  S_location <- apply(
    location_bootstrap_data,
    MARGIN = 1,
    FUN = mad_unscaled
  )

  UCL_L_location <- fast_quantile(
    L_location,
    probs = ucl_probability
  )

  UCL_S_location <- fast_quantile(
    S_location,
    probs = ucl_probability
  )

  # ------------------------------------------------------------
  # Step 5. Event-level bootstrap.
  #
  # Resample the 100 observed event indices with replacement.
  # The corresponding L_t and S_t values remain paired.
  #
  # Each sampled index therefore represents one resampled
  # complete historical event.
  # ------------------------------------------------------------

  set.seed(seed + 2L)

  event_bootstrap_indices <- sample(
    x = seq_len(n_historical_events),
    size = B,
    replace = TRUE
  )

  L_event <- L_observed[
    event_bootstrap_indices
  ]

  S_event <- S_observed[
    event_bootstrap_indices
  ]

  UCL_L_event <- fast_quantile(
    L_event,
    probs = ucl_probability
  )

  UCL_S_event <- fast_quantile(
    S_event,
    probs = ucl_probability
  )

  # ------------------------------------------------------------
  # Step 6. Compare the location-stratified and event-level UCLs.
  #
  # Delta < 0 means that the location-stratified bootstrap gives
  # a smaller UCL than the event-level bootstrap.
  # ------------------------------------------------------------

  Delta_L <-
    UCL_L_location -
    UCL_L_event

  Delta_S <-
    UCL_S_location -
    UCL_S_event

  Percent_Delta_L <-
    100 * Delta_L /
    UCL_L_event

  Percent_Delta_S <-
    100 * Delta_S /
    UCL_S_event

  comparison_table <- data.frame(
    Statistic = c(
      "L",
      "S"
    ),

    UCL_event = c(
      UCL_L_event,
      UCL_S_event
    ),

    UCL_location = c(
      UCL_L_location,
      UCL_S_location
    ),

    Delta = c(
      Delta_L,
      Delta_S
    ),

    Percent_Delta = c(
      Percent_Delta_L,
      Percent_Delta_S
    ),

    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )

  # ------------------------------------------------------------
  # Step 7. Calculate the empirical covariance and correlation
  # matrices of the 10 locations.
  # ------------------------------------------------------------

  empirical_covariance <-
    stats::cov(
      historical_data
    )

  empirical_correlation <-
    stats::cor(
      historical_data
    )

  # ------------------------------------------------------------
  # Return all useful objects.
  # ------------------------------------------------------------

  result <- list(
    seed =
      seed,

    n_historical_events =
      n_historical_events,

    n_locations =
      n_locations,

    location_means =
      location_means,

    event_variance =
      event_variance,

    residual_variance =
      residual_variance,

    marginal_variance =
      marginal_variance,

    marginal_sd =
      marginal_sd,

    theoretical_within_event_correlation =
      within_event_correlation,

    B =
      B,

    target_ARL0 =
      target_ARL0,

    alpha =
      alpha,

    ucl_probability =
      ucl_probability,

    historical_data =
      historical_data,

    event_effects =
      event_effects,

    location_strata =
      location_strata,

    observed_event_statistics =
      observed_event_statistics,

    location_bootstrap_statistics =
      data.frame(
        L_location = L_location,
        S_location = S_location
      ),

    event_bootstrap_statistics =
      data.frame(
        L_event = L_event,
        S_event = S_event
      ),

    empirical_covariance =
      empirical_covariance,

    empirical_correlation =
      empirical_correlation,

    UCL_L_event =
      UCL_L_event,

    UCL_S_event =
      UCL_S_event,

    UCL_L_location =
      UCL_L_location,

    UCL_S_location =
      UCL_S_location,

    comparison_table =
      comparison_table
  )

  class(result) <- c(
    "simulate_event_location_ucl",
    "list"
  )

  print(comparison_table)

  return(result)
}
```
